source_name: Dun & Bradstreet company profile — ASSECO SEE SH.P.K. (Kosovo)
why_relevant: Corroborates the existence, address and rough scale of a global banking vendor's Kosovo legal entity — the corporate-registry-side confirmation of a vendor presence that vendor marketing pages may not spell out per country. Applies as a template to other vendors (Printec, Comtrade, Payten).

source_name: OpenWay Group — blog and customer announcements (Way4 card management)
why_relevant: Way4 is one of the two card-management platforms that dominate the region's issuing/acquiring processors; OpenWay publishes named customer wins (e.g. Nexi). No Kosovo-named reference was found, but the blog is the canonical disclosure channel should a Kosovo bank or a processor serving Kosovo go live, and its regional customers are a route into Kosovo via processing outsourcing.

source_name: Nexi Central Europe — about/newsroom (regional acquiring & processing)
why_relevant: Post Nets/SIA/Nexi consolidation, Nexi Central Europe is a candidate processor/acquirer for South-East European markets; its country and partner-bank disclosures are where a Kosovo processing relationship would surface. Currently no Kosovo-named reference found — monitoring target.

source_name: Horizon Plus — case study: modernizing the Central Bank of Kosovo's digital platform
why_relevant: A vendor case study that names a Kosovo financial institution (the CBK) with scope, technology and strategic context (alignment to the CBK Strategic Plan 2024-2028). Not core banking, but it is exactly the artefact type this cell hunts and demonstrates that smaller local/regional digital agencies publish named Kosovo financial-sector references that the big vendors do not.

source_name: Temenos — customer stories / partner ecosystem
why_relevant: Temenos T24/Transact is the most likely core platform behind several Kosovo banks (a technographics aggregator attributes T24 to Raiffeisen Bank Kosova, and Temenos has published Western Balkans go-lives such as Raiffeisen Bank Bosnia-Herzegovina). Its customer-story library and regional partner list are the primary place a Kosovo go-live plus integrator would be named.

source_name: Bank customer notices of core-system upgrades (BKT Kosova example)
why_relevant: Banks announce planned core-system upgrade/migration windows to customers in Albanian. These notices date core-system events precisely even when the vendor is unnamed, giving a timeline against which vendor claims and RFPs can be matched — a reveals-indirectly source complementing the vendor-side pointer cell.

source_name: Asseco Case Study Book (banking & payment chapters)
why_relevant: Group-level, downloadable PDF compendium of Asseco banking and payment references across CEE/SEE. Best single artefact for identifying whether any Kosovo institution appears in the Asseco reference base and for mapping which product (digital banking, card, PKI/e-signature) went where.

source_name: BIAN case study: Asseco SEE (standards-body customer reference)
why_relevant: Industry standards bodies (BIAN, SWIFT, EMVCo, Mastercard/Visa partner programmes) publish vendor case studies that describe deployed architectures and sometimes name the client banks. A neutral-venue corroboration channel for vendor claims about SEE banking deployments.

source_name: ASEE (Asseco South Eastern Europe) — corporate site, news & group structure
why_relevant: ASEE is the largest regional banking-IT integrator in SEE and runs a registered Kosovo entity (Asseco SEE sh.p.k., Prishtina). Its news/case-study stream and group-structure page name banking and payments deals across Serbia, Croatia, North Macedonia and Kosovo, and are the single best window on the competitor most likely to be incumbent in a Kosovo bank.

source_name: Payten (ASEE payments arm) — news & offering pages
why_relevant: Payten is the ASEE payments/ATM/POS business and the most direct regional competitor for card acceptance, ATM managed services and processing in the Western Balkans. Its news section publishes named bank contracts (e.g. Erste Croatia ATM delivery, unattended POS in Serbia) that indicate the territory model under which Kosovo is served.

source_name: Comtrade Computers Kosovo (Comtrade System Integration / Adriatic)
why_relevant: Serbian/Slovenian-rooted Comtrade operates a Prishtina entity and its profile explicitly names Kosovo banking clients (Banka Kreditore e Prishtinës, Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo, Kasabank, and the former Banking and Payments Authority of Kosovo). That is a rare, concrete Kosovo reference list for a regional integrator.

source_name: Halcom — regional e-banking vendor, markets & bank-user lists
why_relevant: Halcom (Slovenia) lists Kosovo among its ~10 markets and its own history states it launched the first mobile bank at Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo (2011). Its support pages publish per-country lists of banks using Hal E-Bank — effectively a ready-made installed-base map for corporate e-banking in the region.

source_name: Halcom Slovenian-language newsroom (halcom.si / halcom.com/sl)
why_relevant: Slovenian- and Serbian-language Halcom news items carry regional detail (anniversaries, market entries, bank partnerships) that the English site omits. Useful as the local-language mirror for tracking when Halcom expands or loses a Western Balkans bank.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. — Slovenian card processor serving Kosovo, incl. annual reports
source_subtype: processor corporate site + audited annual reports (PDF)
why_relevant: Bankart explicitly states it processes cards for banks in Slovenia, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia and Montenegro — i.e. part of Kosovo's card processing is outsourced across the border. Its published annual reports quantify volumes and name platform vendors (its 2022-24 tender went to Diebold Nixdorf), which is directly competitive intelligence on the processing layer.

source_name: InfoSoft Systems Kosovo (InfoSoft Group Albania) — company & partner pages
why_relevant: InfoSoft is the Albanian IT group that entered Kosovo (Prishtina, 2014) and North Macedonia — the textbook Albania→Kosovo channel. It is a named BankFlex integration partner for Albania and neighbouring countries and lists ProCredit Bank among clients, making it a probable bidder against any banking-software proposal in Kosovo.

source_name: BankFlex (Eon Technologies) partner/news archive — regional integration partners
why_relevant: Product vendors that sell through Balkan integrators publish partner announcements naming who carries them into Albania/Kosovo. The BankFlex archive is the record of the InfoSoft partnership and is a template for finding other 'vendor + local integrator' pairs that never surface in Kosovo-only searches.

source_name: Nextsense (Skopje) — regional digital/identity & banking solutions vendor
why_relevant: North Macedonian vendor active in finance and government digitalisation across the region, and a Thales partner (a relevant signal for card/HSM/digital-signature work). Its partner listings and profiles are the entry point for tracing whether it carries Kosovo bank references.

source_name: Thales CPL partner directory (regional integrator listings)
why_relevant: OEM partner directories are the most reliable way to enumerate which Balkan integrators are certified to resell payment-security, HSM and authentication products — a proxy for who can credibly bid on Kosovo bank security/payments work. Searchable by country.

source_name: Progress/Kemp-style OEM partner locators (example: Kemp partner page for InfoSoft Systems)
why_relevant: Infrastructure-vendor partner locators confirm which legal entity in which country holds the reseller status, and often expose the Kosovo/Albania/Macedonia entity split of a group. Cheap corroboration for the channel map.

source_name: Saga d.o.o. Beograd — Serbian banking integrator, partnership announcements
why_relevant: Saga is one of Serbia's leading banking-IT houses with subsidiaries in Montenegro, BiH and North Macedonia, and has publicly partnered with Salt Edge on open-banking/PSD2 for Serbian banks. Its regional footprint makes it a plausible bidder wherever a Serbian-owned or Serbian-language bank operates in the Kosovo territory.

source_name: Salt Edge partner/news blog — regional open-banking integrator pairings
why_relevant: Open-banking enablers publish which local integrator they signed for each Balkan market. That reveals who is positioned to win PSD2/open-banking work in Kosovo once the CBK payments law lands, and which regional partner already owns the bank relationship.

source_name: Intracom Telecom — international offices, success stories and press archive
why_relevant: Greek-rooted Intracom serves Kosovo through Intracom Skopje and an Albanian entity, and its Kosovo track record (e.g. a 2005 PTK contract) shows the Skopje-serves-Kosovo pattern. Its press archive and success stories are how any move into financial-sector or payments infrastructure would first surface.

source_name: OpenCorporates.al — Albanian company register mirror (NIPT lookups)
why_relevant: Albanian-language registry data resolves the legal identity, ownership and name changes of Albanian entities of regional integrators (e.g. Intracom Telecom Albania, ex-Intralban). Essential for de-duplicating aliases and for tracing which Albanian entity actually fronts Kosovo work.

source_name: Dun & Bradstreet business-directory profiles for Kosovo/regional IT subsidiaries
why_relevant: D&B profiles exist for the Kosovo subsidiaries of regional integrators (Asseco SEE sh.p.k., Comtrade Computers sh.p.k., Nextsense d.o.o.) and give headcount, revenue estimate and corporate-family linkage — the quickest way to size a competitor's Kosovo presence when the vendor publishes nothing itself.

source_name: e-Prokurimi — Kosovo public e-procurement portal (with open data API)
why_relevant: Kosovo publishes tender dossiers, bidder lists, signed contracts and supplier names across the full procurement cycle, with an API added in 2021. Awards to Albanian, Macedonian or Serbian IT suppliers reveal which regional integrators actually operate in Kosovo and at what contract values — evidence not available from vendor marketing. Covers public bodies (incl. state entities) rather than commercial banks, so treat as adjacent evidence.

source_name: LinkedIn company pages of regional integrators (Kosovo/regional entities)
why_relevant: For integrators with thin or stale websites, the LinkedIn page is the live signal: Kosovo job postings, project posts, and named bank client mentions. It is often the only place a Kosovo delivery team is visible for a company headquartered in Belgrade, Skopje, Tirana or Zagreb.

source_name: Kosovo bank vendor-facing pages as reverse-lookup evidence (e.g. Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo digital services)
why_relevant: Bank product pages (RaiPay wallet, ATM services, e-banking) expose the underlying platform brands and thus, by reverse lookup, which regional integrator supplied them. This is the practical way to attribute an installed base when neither the bank nor the vendor issues a press release.

source_name: KosovaJob.com — Kosovo job board (bank/IT vacancies)
why_relevant: Largest Kosovo job network; banks (BKT Kosova, NLB, Credins, ProCredit, TEB) and IT vendors post role descriptions that name the core banking / card / channel systems the hire will operate. Employer profile pages aggregate a single bank's postings over time, enabling stack and migration-burst tracking.
